article.title: Ter + particípio y el aspecto perfect en portugués brasileño y español de Madrid
article.part: Contraste Guatemala–Brasil y dominio avanzado C1–C2 — Contraste Guatemala–Brasil e domínio avançado C1–C2
article.chapter: Contraste español de Guatemala–portugués de Brasil — Contraste espanhol da Guatemala–português do Brasil

claims.summary: The source defines universal perfect as relating a past situation to the present through persistence and existential perfect through effects.
The comparative study concludes that ter + participle does not behave uniformly in Brazilian Portuguese and Madrid Spanish.
The study identifies other verbal forms and adverbs/adverbial expressions as contributing to perfect aspect in both varieties.

The cited comparison concerns Brazilian Portuguese and Madrid Spanish and is based on a review of descriptions in the literature, so it does not establish a uniform rule across all verbs, contexts or Spanish varieties.
